entries.title: C0120 source scope (draft audit)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. Let g_v be independent N(0,1) weights on Z^2 and let M_n maximize their sum over n-vertex paths from (0,0) with east/north unit steps and free endpoint. The cited Chatterjee 2008 Theorem 8.1 gives Var(M_n)<=C n/log n. The source-faithful power target is Var(M_n)<=C n^(1-epsilon), epsilon>0. The cited theorem does not state the intake's general-dimension log-partition formulation. Present openness UNKNOWN.

entries.title: Gaussian maximum variance controls (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. For W_m=max(Z_1,...,Z_m) with independent standard normal Z_i and m>=16, c/log(m)<=Var(W_m)<=2/log(m), where c=(1-exp(-(2/5)*exp(-3/2)))/8. The author proof uses Mills bounds, two separated quantile events, and finite-dimensional Gaussian OU hypercontractivity; see ATTEMPT.md L1.

entries.title: Binary-tree and private-chains polymer (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. For r>=1 and m=n=2^r, put independent N(0,1) weights on a complete binary tree's internal levels 0,...,r-1 and on m private n-vertex chains at its leaf positions. Orient edges away from the root. Every root-to-terminal path has L=n+r vertices; indegree is at most 1 and outdegree at most 2. Let U_i be the internal prefix, S_i the private-chain sum, M=max_i(U_i+S_i), and A=max_i S_i. This graph family is not the fixed east/north lattice. The author bound is E[(M-A)^2]<=2r(log(2m)+1).

entries.title: Bounded first chaos on tree and chains (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. For the binary-tree-plus-private-chains model with m=n=2^r and L=n+r, the first Gaussian-chaos projection Pi_1 M=sum_v E[M g_v]g_v has variance exactly 3-2/m. Almost surely every coordinate derivative of M is 0 or 1 and the total squared gradient is L. Coefficients are 2^-k at each internal vertex on level k and 1/m on each chain vertex, by transitivity and Gaussian integration by parts.
assumptions: Finite model defined in this bundle

entries.title: Power variance inference obstruction (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. For the binary-tree-plus-private-chains Gaussian model, Var(M)=Theta(L/log L) as r grows although Var(Pi_1 M)<3, every derivative is bounded by 1, all paths have L vertices, the root is common, and outdegree is at most 2. Explicitly, c n/(4 log m)<=Var(M)<6n/log m whenever 2r(log(2m)+1)<=c n/(4 log m), with m=n=2^r, L=n+r and c=(1-exp(-(2/5)*exp(-3/2)))/8. These properties alone do not imply a positive power saving. This is not a counterexample on the source lattice.

entries.title: Fixed temperature obstruction (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. In the same Gaussian graph family, for each fixed beta>0, F_beta=beta^-1 log[m^-1 sum_i exp(beta(U_i+S_i))] has Var(F_beta)=Theta(L/log L) as r grows and first Gaussian-chaos variance 3-2/m. The deterministic comparison is M-log(m)/beta<=F_beta<=M. This is a graph-family statement, not a theorem for the original lattice or for beta varying with r.

entries.title: Remaining C0120 lattice gap (draft)
entries.statement: DRAFT; author proof or source audit only; independent review pending. The independent attempt does not solve C0120. A power variance gain for the fixed east/north lattice requires a justified quantitative estimate controlling the higher Gaussian chaoses or noise overlap. The obstruction graph has 2^r vertices at layer r, versus r+1 for the source lattice, and lacks its reconvergence. Small first chaos and bounded outdegree alone leave this gap open.
assumptions: No parent solved or novelty claim

relations.rationale: The exact coefficient sum uses the model's r internal levels and m private n-vertex chains.
The variance comparison uses E[(M-A)^2]<=2r(log(2m)+1) in this specific graph family.
The private-chain maximum has law sqrt(n) W_m; the explicit logarithmic variance bounds transfer through the prefix error.
The simultaneous first-chaos variance 3-2/m and total variance Theta(L/log L) invalidate the abstract implication.
The Gibbs sum is over the same m equal-length root-to-terminal paths.
The log-sum-exp comparison produces the same logarithmic variance obstruction for each fixed beta>0.
The graph obstruction shows why bounded degree and first-chaos smallness do not discharge the parent lattice estimate.
Both refer explicitly to C0120's fixed Gaussian east/north ground-state model, with present openness UNKNOWN.
